title: Analysis: SDF Has Dissolved, But Syria's Military Unity Remains in Question
detail: While the Kurdish-led SDF formally announced its dissolution and merger into the Syrian national army on August 25, analysts and observers are raising significant questions about whether Syria has truly achieved a unified military command. The SDF's integration was completed on paper, but deep structural divisions persist: Kurdish fighters retain distinct cultural identities, chain-of-command ambiguities remain between former SDF units and the HTS-rooted command, and US forces' future role in northeast Syria is unresolved. The agreement grants Kurdish civil and educational rights but leaves unresolved how those commitments will be enforced within a centralized Syrian state. The formal dissolution announcement followed the January 2026 merger deal and August 21 civil-institution integration, but observers note that symbolic unification and operational integration are two different milestones.

media.caption: Questions persist over Syria's true military unification after the formal SDF dissolution
